I have figured out how to perform an SEM and growth curve separately but not how
to do it in one model.
It will be very much appreciated if anyone can give me advice on how to code a
growth curve as modeled above or improvements I can make on the coding I did.

My model looks like this.

The y(AE), time-varying covariates TVC1(AS) and TVC2(TC) are latent variables measured
by 5 survey items (AE and AS) and 4 items (TC) measured across 9 time-points.
(the pic attached shows only 5 time-points but the pattern is the same)
The TIC1 is country and TIC2 is classes per week.
The code I created is in the attatched doc file.

I am still very new to lavaan. It'll be great if anyone can lend me a hand to get to
know it better.

Best regards,

Emiko

#Time Varying Constructs (TC)

              T1_ae~T1_tc                   #how T1 tc affects T1,T2 ae

              T2_ae~T1_tc

              T8_ae~T7_tc

              T9_ae~T8_tc

       '

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Coding for a GCM which the outcome variable is latent
parts:
Latent means are fixed to 0 by default for identification.  Before you fit a GCM, just fit a longitudinal CFA and evaluate measurement invariance.  If you can impose (at least partial) scalar invariance constraints, then the equality of indicator intercepts will allow you to estimate all but one occasion's latent mean.  For example, the first occasion can remain fixed to 0 for identification.  Any change in means can then be modeled by the GCM, in which the scalar-invariance constraints are in place but all latent means are fixed to zero.  The mean of the slope factor can be estimated, but the mean of the latent intercept factor must be fixed to zero, consistent with the first-occasion's latent mean being zero for identification.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
